record_before.short_name: CA SB 79 (Tier 1 stop, 1/4 to 1/2 mile, city of 35,000+)
record_before.statute_citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 65912.155 et seq. (Chapter 4.1.5; § 65912.157 as amended by SB 722, Stats. 2026, ch. 100)
record_before.summary: Between 1/4 and 1/2 mile of a Tier 1 stop, in a city of at least 35,000: height floor 65 ft, density floor 100 dwelling units per acre, 3.0 FAR. Tier 2 stops (light rail, high-frequency commuter rail, qualifying bus) get 65 ft/100 du/ac/3.0 within 1/4 mile and 55 ft/80 du/ac/2.5 at 1/4-1/2 mile (not modelled).
record_before.effective_date_note: Code section effective 2026-01-01; bill digest: provisions "would not apply to a local agency until July 1, 2026, except as specified, or within unincorporated areas of counties until the 7th regional housing needs allocation cycle"
record_before.eligible_counties_note: Statute applies to any "urban transit county" (county with more than 15 passenger rail stations), not a fixed list; the previous 9-county list is not in the statute and is unconfirmed
record_before.min_parking_note: SB 79 chaptered text contains no parking-minimum elimination; parking ratios come from Gov. Code 65915 density bonus law
record_before.affordability_note: 65912.157(i) offers alternatives (e.g. 7% extremely low, 10% very low income units); a single percentage is not statutory
record_before.statutory_exclusions_note: Chapter incorporates Gov. Code 65913.4 (very high fire hazard severity zone bar) when streamlining is sought; historic/sea-level-rise sites may be excluded from density rules up to 10% of eligible area; HPOZ/coastal-commission/floodway list in earlier record is not in SB 79 text
